# gcore_waap_domain_custom_rules (Data Source)

WAAP custom rules allow, block, challenge, monitor or tag requests to a domain when all of their conditions match.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gcore_waap_domain_custom_rules" "example_waap_domain_custom_rules" {
  domain_id = 1
  action = "block"
  description = "This rule blocks all the requests coming form a specific IP address."
  enabled = false
  name = "Block by specific IP rule."
  ordering = "-id"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (Number) The domain ID

### Optional

- `action` (String) Filter to refine results by specific actions
Available values: "allow", "block", "captcha", "handshake", "monitor", "tag".
- `description` (String) Filter rules based on their description. Supports '*' as a wildcard character.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Filter rules based on their active status
- `max_items` (Number) Max items to fetch, default: 1000
- `name` (String) Filter rules based on their name. Supports '*' as a wildcard character.
- `ordering` (String) Determine the field to order results by
Available values: "id", "name", "description", "enabled", "action", "-id", "-name", "-description", "-enabled", "-action".

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) The items returned by the data source (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `action` (Attributes) The action that the rule takes when triggered. Only one action can be set per rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--action))
- `conditions` (Attributes List) The conditions required for the WAAP engine to trigger the rule. Rules may have between 1 and 5 conditions. All conditions must pass for the rule to trigger (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions))
- `description` (String) A human-readable description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether or not the rule is enabled
- `id` (Number) The unique identifier for the rule
- `name` (String) The name assigned to the rule

<a id="nestedatt--items--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.action`

Read-Only:

- `allow` (Map of String) The WAAP allows the request
- `block` (Attributes) WAAP block action behavior could be configured with response status code and action duration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--action--block))
- `captcha` (Map of String) The WAAP presents the user with a captcha
- `handshake` (Map of String) The WAAP performs automatic browser validation
- `monitor` (Map of String) The WAAP monitors the request but takes no action
- `tag` (Attributes) WAAP tag action gets a list of tags to tag the request scope with (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--action--tag))

<a id="nestedatt--items--action--block"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.action.block`

Read-Only:

- `action_duration` (String) How long a rule's block action will apply to subsequent requests. Can be specified in seconds or by using a numeral followed by 's', 'm', 'h', or 'd' to represent time format (seconds, minutes, hours, or days). Empty time intervals are not allowed. If not specified, the action is applied only to the request that triggers the rule.
- `status_code` (Number) An HTTP status code that the WAAP returns if a rule blocks a request.
Available values: 403, 405, 418, 429.


<a id="nestedatt--items--action--tag"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.action.tag`

Read-Only:

- `tags` (Set of String) The list of user defined tags to tag the request with



<a id="nestedatt--items--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.conditions`

Read-Only:

- `asn` (Attributes) Match the ASN (Autonomous System Number) the request originated from, as determined by a WHOIS lookup of the requesting IP (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--asn))
- `content_type` (Attributes) Match the requested Content-Type (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--content_type))
- `country` (Attributes) Match the country that the request originated from (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--country))
- `file_extension` (Attributes) Match the incoming file extension (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--file_extension))
- `header` (Attributes) Match an incoming request header (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--header))
- `header_exists` (Attributes) Match when an incoming request header is present (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--header_exists))
- `http_method` (Attributes) Match the incoming HTTP method (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--http_method))
- `ip` (Attributes) Match the incoming request against a single IP address (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--ip))
- `ip_range` (Attributes) Match the incoming request against an IP range (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--ip_range))
- `ja3` (Attributes) Match the JA3 TLS client fingerprint of the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--ja3))
- `ja4` (Attributes) Match the JA4 TLS client fingerprint of the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--ja4))
- `organization` (Attributes) Match the organization the request originated from, as determined by a WHOIS lookup of the requesting IP (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--organization))
- `owner_types` (Attributes) Match the type of organization that owns the IP address making an incoming request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--owner_types))
- `request_rate` (Attributes) Match the rate at which requests come in that match certain conditions (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--request_rate))
- `response_header` (Attributes) Match a response header (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--response_header))
- `response_header_exists` (Attributes) Match when a response header is present (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--response_header_exists))
- `session_request_count` (Attributes) Match the number of dynamic page requests made in a WAAP session (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--session_request_count))
- `tags` (Attributes) Matches requests based on specified tags (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--tags))
- `url` (Attributes) Match the incoming request URL (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--url))
- `user_agent` (Attributes) Match the user agent making the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--user_agent))
- `user_defined_tags` (Attributes) Matches requests based on user-defined tags (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--conditions--user_defined_tags))

<a id="nestedatt--items--conditions--url"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.conditions.url`

Read-Only:

- `match_type` (String) The type of matching condition.
Available values: "Exact", "Contains", "Regex".
- `negation` (Boolean) Whether or not to apply a boolean NOT operation to the rule's condition
- `url` (String) The pattern to match against the request URL.
Constraints depend on `match_type`:

- **Exact/Contains**: plain text matching (e.g., `/admin`, must comply with `^[\w!\$~:#\[\]@\(\)*\+,=\/\-\.\%]+$`).
- **Regex**: a valid regular expression (e.g., `^/upload(/\d+)?/\w+`). Lookahead/lookbehind constructs are forbidden.
